title: Certificates of Deposit: The Savings Balance Available to Fund an In-Term Add-On
content:
When the holder of a PCB certificate (Certificates of Deposit) funds an in-term add-on from a PCB savings or money market account, the account the money leaves sets its own limit. This page states that limit.

## Rule

The room in the source account is the current balance held in the savings or money market account, active and in the owner's name at PCB, from which the add-on is drawn. The add-on can take no more than that balance, because a savings balance is never allowed to fall below zero. The balance is read as it stands when the add-on is made.

An owner holding no active savings or money market account has no balance to draw on, and the room from this source is nil.

## Cases (hypothetical balances)

| Owner's active savings or money market account | Room in the source account |
|---|---|
| Statement Savings, current balance USD 18250.40 | USD 18250.40 |
| Money Market Account, current balance USD 3000.00 | USD 3000.00 |
| Only a closed savings account | nil |

## Point of judgement

**Can the owner's savings go overdrawn to complete a larger add-on?** No. The balance on hand is the most this source can supply.
